java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.Result.Missing<T>
Type Parameters:

Record Components:

    Methods inherited from interface LogProperty.Result

    validate, validateIfError, validateNow
    Modifier and Type
    Method
    Description
    default LogProperty.ValidatedResult<T>
    validate(LogProperty.Validator validator)
    Registers this result with validator via LogProperty.Validator.add(Result) (a still-LogProperty.Result.Missing result is treated as a real failure) and returns this result unchanged, so a chain that builds a required property can register itself with a shared LogProperty.Validator and keep going in one expression - properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validate(v) - instead of a separate var x = ...; v.add(x); statement pair.
    default LogProperty.ValidatedResult<T>
    validateIfError(LogProperty.Validator validator)
    Like LogProperty.Result.validate(Validator) but via LogProperty.Validator.addIfError(Result) instead of LogProperty.Validator.add(Result) - a LogProperty.Result.Missing result is expected and ignored, only a LogProperty.Result.Error is treated as a failure.
    default T
    validateNow(Class<?> component)
    Convenience for a genuine one-off, single-property validation that does not need to participate in a larger batch: builds a single-use LogProperty.Validator, registers this result with it via LogProperty.Validator.add(Result), and validates immediately - instead of registering with a caller-managed LogProperty.Validator via LogProperty.Result.validate(Validator) and deferring to a later LogProperty.Validator.validate() call.

    • map

      public <U> LogProperty.Result.Missing<U> map(LogProperty.PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper)
      Description copied from interface: LogProperty.Result
      Maps this result's value through mapper. On success, keeps the origin (topProperties/properties/key/ rawValue/kind, see PropertySuccess) so a later conversion step's error message can still point back to it. On failure, builds a rich error message - which key it came from, where that key was found, and (for LogProperty.PropertyConvertException/LogProperty.ValidationException causes) the original raw value - with a "Tried:" line searching topProperties: the LogProperties the very first LogProperties.forKey(String) in this chain was looked up against, which for a chained/composite LogProperties.of(a, b) can be broader than the exact source the value was actually found at. Usable at any point in a chain, not just directly off a LogProperty, since a LogProperty.Result.Success keeps pointing back to the property it originally came from no matter how many conversions have run since.
      Specified by:
      map in interface LogProperty.Result<T>
      Type Parameters:
      U - result type
      Parameters:
      mapper - mapping function.
      Returns:
      mapped result.
